quest.title: Hunters, Prophets
quest.description: You return to the Spina di Rosula base in Fleuve Cendre, and there, you meet an unexpected friend...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Go to the Spina di Rosula base

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Seriously? Nobody just uses a scryglass whenever they've got time to just see who they'll meet on the road.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, we didn't expect to see you here... Wait, you're not a Fontainian, are you, Mona?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Well, I have some business to attend to here, so I booked a hotel in the city. I was just out for a stroll... when I bumped into you. Quite unexpectedly, if I might add.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Why did you think I was from Fontaine, though? Is that because "Megistus" doesn't sound much like a Mondstadter surname?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, let's go with that!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Well, I used to have my own surname, which was, well, some other thing... Either way, the old hag told me when she took me as her disciple that the first step to being a Great Astrologist's pupil was to change that name.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: There was nothing for it, really. She really is amazing at astrology, so I changed my name to what it is now according to her wishes. To my surprise, however, "Megistus" is not the name of some ancient house or clan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? It isn't?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Nope. Although it is used by us in place of surnames, it generally just means "great."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, imagine including a boast in your name... Wait, are you gonna have to put that into your genealogy as well?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I reckon so. In any case, I'd give my disciple a name like this as well, if I were to take one.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And may I ask what your master's name is?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Astromancer Barbeloth Trismegistus.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, that's a long one... Does it also mean "great" or something?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: My name means "Mona, the Great Astrologist." As for the old hag, hers is, in plain speech, "the thrice-as-great scholar of the stars." Just take it as a title specific to astrologists.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thrice-as-great!? That's so... petty!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I know, right? That's just how she is! She used to call herself Megistus, actually, but once she took me in, she changed her name to Trismegistus...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Talk about excessive...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Megistus is thus the calling card of our school, so to speak, which makes it about the same as a surname. It's alright if you don't get it — you can look into it further should you need to study astrology more deeply.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds terrible!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But anyway, you're not Fontainian, are you, Mona? You're from Mondstadt, right?

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Well, I was born in Mondstadt, yes. My parents migrated to Dornman Port, and I traveled with the old hag for a while, after which I settled down in Mondstadt City.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's a good thing then! At least we know you won't be dissolved by Fontaine's waters.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Hmm, speaking of that, I'm sure you're aware that a bunch of things have happened here in Fontaine, right? I know you're not a local, but I'd avoid getting too close to any water that looks strange all the same.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: There's something ominous about it... The water, I mean.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did you come to Fontaine because of the prophecy, Mona?

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: That was the main reason, yes. Just a while back, The Steambird invited me to take part in a panel and speak about the circulation of the prophecy as an astrologist.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: The invitation was sent quite early on. I don't think anyone expected Fontaine to be in this much trouble.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you make of that prophecy, Mona? Just tell us what you think as an astrologist... Your word would go a long way to make things more certain and less... scary!

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: What I can tell you is that I'm an astrologist, and that this prophecy concerns the fate of Fontaine, even that of all Teyvat. Ascertaining this is akin to reading the fortune of the whole world.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: I'm afraid that this is not something that just anyone can do. If I could do it, you would no longer call me an astrologist... but a visionary.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: But on the flip side, the prophecy is so huge and powerful that it must surely come from a powerful visionary. Its contents involve the fate of the world... Disregarding it would be a mistake.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A visionary... Sounds really powerful and all, but does such a person really exist?

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Of course. The old hag could do it, and I'd bet there are others amongst those Hexenzirkel colleagues of hers who could do something similar.

choices.text: I need to ascertain the accuracy of the prophecy.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Huh? A—Are you sure?

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Hmm... Alright, I'll help you. It isn't often that I see you with such a serious look on your face. I'll tell you once I hear back from her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks, Mona! You're amazing as always.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Hehe. Well, this is something only I can do, after all. So yes, your praises are quite welcome!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's the greatest of astrologists for you! Of all the people we know, you know the stars the best.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Indeed, indeed! That's the spirit.

response.speaker: Tetreaux
response.text: Oh, sorry. I came to see what all the commotion was about... If there is anything you need, do not hesitate to inform the Spina di Rosula.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Uh... Whoops, guess we were getting a little too carried away there. Well, I'll go tend to my own business now. If I receive any news, I'll be sure to come find you two again!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And there she goes, quick as rushing water... And here we are with this Spina guy giving us suspicious looks.

choices.text: Well, we were making a ruckus.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, but we were able to recruit Mona's help, didn't we? Our Fontainian friends will thank us someday.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After the conversation, you decide to get a good night's sleep to replenish your energy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *yawn* Good morning... To be honest, Paimon's still feeling kinda sleepy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But it's time to get up, Traveler! We agreed to go see Neuvillette, so let's pack it up and get going.

choices.text: Try to keep it down next time, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hah! If Paimon hadn't spoken for you, it'd be you getting all the weird looks! Hmph. The things Paimon does for you...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Alright, alright. Thanks, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe... That's more like it!

choices.text: Could you help me get in touch with your master?

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: Y—You're here! Finally!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: Monsieur Neuvillette and Lady Furina... they seem to have gotten into a dispute! Please, go see for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Like I said, I've already explained everything!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: And yet, the problem has not been properly solved. There is little space for excuses between us.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: It is not my intention to offend you, but please, tell me where you stand. You are the Hydro Archon Focalors, are you not?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Look at this. This is a list of the victims from the recent Poisson incident.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Y—You mean... They're all...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: We did not arrive in time to avert this disaster, and I will not have it happen again.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I will say this once more. You must tell me everything you know.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Yesterday, I found three stone slates in some ancient ruins near Poisson. Do you know anything about those?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...Seriously? You're questioning me like this is a court case now. I don't know anything about that.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: But... you found them in some ancient ruins, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: That's correct, which is why I came to ask you some questions. There should have been four slates, but one of them was missing. The other three feature different images that seem to correlate to the prophecy.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: The prophecy...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The second of these slates depicts the previous Hydro Archon Egeria kneeling before a floating island in the sky, as if confessing something. Do you know nothing of this, either?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I don't. I've never seen such slates.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I'll ask you again... Do you really have no information regarding the previous Archon?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: My deciphering of the slates indicates that the Hydro Archon Egeria once had to confess to, or apologize for, a certain sin. If anyone would know about it, it should be you.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: All gods don't have the same secrets, you know. She was herself, and I'm me. Is it really so strange that I know nothing?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I understand your concerns, but... I'm sorry. I just don't have anything to tell you.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Forgive me for saying this now, Lady Furina, but I have long known of your various secret investigations into certain matters.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: There are several indications that you have been investigating the prophecy on the sly.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: This is not strange in itself, considering that you are the Hydro Archon. But it is strange that you also should claim not to know any of Egeria's secrets, as well as do nothing following your inquiries.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: You have never been as superficial as you have presented yourself to be, nor are you a fool. And yet, your behavior is very inconsistent...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Haha... Hahahaha! So you've been watching me all this time, have you? I didn't think you were that type!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: You...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Well, since you know about my secret investigations, then you should know I'm actually working to take care of it.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: There's no point questioning or suspecting me. You're the Iudex, but you're still my subordinate — you should be following my lead.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Just trust in me, your Archon, and do as I say — never mind whether you can truly convince yourself to or not. It'll all turn out fine.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...That's all I have to say. We do not discuss this matter again.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ah, the opera's about to start. Toodles!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did Furina not notice us standing by the door? Wonder what's up with her. She was smiling... Huh, she didn't seem in the mood to care if we were listening in or not...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I assume you've been outside for a while now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you noticed? Seems Furina didn't even realize we were here.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: She was in a great panic, though I cannot discern the reason. Our discussion reached impasses time and again — a state of affairs that we cannot allow to continue.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Still, I do not understand. Dialogue is the basis for understanding, so why did she keep refusing to engage?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm afraid questions alone might not suffice...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We need to make her understand how dire the situation actually is.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Everyone in her inner circle has noticed that she is hiding some secret. The issue is her attitude. I fear that she will not reveal anything unless absolutely forced to.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: We may have to create a situation in which she will have no choice but to speak.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? Like what?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Normally, people will only reveal the truth when standing trial. Perhaps we must have the Hydro Archon experience just such a scenario.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Furina's seen so many trials, and she's really good at dodging questions. How do we make sure that she won't just slip away at the first chance she gets?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: We will need to consider this thoroughly, join forces with various parties, and then do what we can.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: If at all possible, I would prefer to recuse myself from this affair, but... We must prevent the prophecy from coming to pass.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: This may be cruel to her, but all Fontaine is in crisis — the "information a god possesses" is too precious, and so we must take a chance on this.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: In that case, we will need help.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: But who will lend us their aid to do such a thing?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh, I think I know who to call.

choices.text: She seems to be deliberately hiding something...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lady Megistus!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that's everyone, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, it was pretty smart of you to think of hiding here.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Poisson was just involved in a disaster, so it's presently devoid of people. That naturally makes it the best choice.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And here you are, drinking tea like it's the most natural thing in the world, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: That's what family should do — sit and enjoy a leisurely time together.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Haha. It's nice to enjoy tea here, you know. Care for a cup?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ahem! Lend me your ears, everyone... Hmm. Or perhaps one of you might like to start us off? How about you, friend?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Uh, me!? N—No, I don't think I can...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Then, how about you, good sir?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I fear that I will cause the mood on this boat to become as somber as it is in court...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well then, I guess we're lucky we've got a local like me to organize things. Wonderful — the spotlight, at last! I guess I'll be facilitating things from here.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: That was a little long-winded, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #Oh, you might be right... Anyway, to cut to the chase, our friend here, {NICKNAME}, has brought us together to discuss something.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: As for what that is... Well, let's start by saying that we'll be pooling our efforts together to create a series of "traps."

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oh? How intriguing.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, it's just an expression, really — one that I just learned from Clorinde, and used on the spot... so let's invite her to explain in detail. A round of applause, please!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Huh? Didn't you say that you would be facilitating this?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, come now, your work doesn't involve much public speaking, right? This is a good chance to practice — you might even pick up some fancy oratory tricks to impress your boss with in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I see. And what does my boss say?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Ahem... He is glad that you consider him your boss. Do go on.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: In that case, do any of you have experience in... hunting?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Not that I recall.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Freminet and I once used a wooden stick and a basket to catch wild rabbits when we were younger. As for Lynette... Ah right, you were sick that day, weren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I've also gone diving to catch some fish before. Does that count?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I'm afraid not. You may or may not have heard, but Fontaine once played host to a group known as the Marechaussee Hunters.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Though that was their name, they did not hunt animals, but rather various monsters left behind by the ancient dynasty of King Remus.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Today, Fontaine's monster population has already thinned greatly, so the Hunters have blended back into society, taking up arms in other lines of work. They even left a unique methodology of hunting in their wake.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: A trap comprises of the following components: bait, a trigger, and a containment device. Sometimes, a lethal implement will also be necessary to deal with the prey.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: So if we were to build a trap together right now, what would you choose to build it with?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: For me, I would prefer something basket-shaped. Pigeons and rabbits will see the bait and naturally enter the snare.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Our line of work requires a deft hand, and we're some of the best in the industry, so you can count on our techniques.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You used some of those techniques while moving the people of Poisson, didn't you? My subordinates mentioned that you even performed some magic for the bawling children.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Yes, and I even managed to gather some intelligence in the meantime — I'm quite the multitasker if I do say so myself.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I can't claim that as my strong suit... I prefer more stable methods, like placing bait in the water and waiting for the fish to come within reach... That's the kind of method I would count on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, calm and steady — exactly the kind of person who would catch loads of fish.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: And I can be their assistant.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: With discretion, I'm sure.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hmm... I'd probably use some sort of mechanical animal. Papa once bought me some small clockwork squirrels, mice, and such. When placed in the forest, they can attract others of their kind.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I remember that you liked those too, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I did, and that would be a good way to go about it. If they're realistic enough, animals of the same kind will follow them all the way to the trap.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What about you, Monsieur Neuvillette?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I... fear I do not have any related experience.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: That makes sense. You usually solve problems directly, without the use of any such tricks.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: But I do have one more question for you, Monsieur.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: If we were to create a trap now, how would you design it?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Hmm, I would like for it to be effective but bring no harm to the prey. A more gentle trap would be ideal.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Kind, as always. However, our intention doesn't necessarily change the containment device and the type of implement we need.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: If we wanted to kill the prey in one strike, we would need a powerful implement. However, that also goes for prey that must be captured and safely contained.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Wait, why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Only a hunter who is a true expert at subduing their prey can snare it without harming it. The line that divides life and death is often exceedingly thin.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: ...So, are we going hunting together?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, we hadn't thought of seeing ourselves as hunters. It kinda works... but maybe it's still not the best metaphor.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: If our means of capturing and dealing with our prey is to put them on trial, then the hunting metaphor is actually quite accurate.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: But we shall require much more courage than any hunter to judge a god — a being whose seat is an exalted throne.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's what is going on... sounds very interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Clorinde's hunting metaphor was just that... a metaphor.\nYou will not call this a "hunt" because that is not what you should do at present, nor has the relationship between you and Furina reached such a dire stage.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: What you need is simply the secrets she is keeping.\nAttempting to take her secrets is an act of sacrilegious disrespect, but must be done to prevent Fontaine from sinking into the waters as foretold in the prophecy.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: There is neither hunter nor prey, but there must be a "trap."\nThat is what you will need.

talks.objective: Go to the Spina di Rosula base

dialogues.speaker: Mage "N"
dialogues.text: Ah, so you've caught on.

dialogues.speaker: Mage "N"
dialogues.text: Just as prophecies are usually only the future as seen from the perspectives of the gods, could things be happening in hidden corners where the gods' gaze does not fall?

dialogues.speaker: Mage "N"
dialogues.text: Are the things that you shall see different from the fate that the gods perceive?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What is she talking about? It all sounds really impressive and important and stuff... but it also sounds kinda scary.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The tea in the teacup is just about gone as well...)

dialogues.speaker: Mage "N"
dialogues.text: I believe that you understand, right? Some things are insignificant... but others, you must reach out to change.

dialogues.speaker: Mage "N"
dialogues.text: Ultimately, fate shall serve as your only guide no matter what will happen in Teyvat's future. All you need to do is to play your part.

dialogues.speaker: Mage "N"
dialogues.text: This was good tea, by the way. Thank you for your hospitality. Well, that'll be all for today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The voice... it's gone.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Mage N... is this the clue you're leaving for us?)

talks.objective: Get out of bed and open the door

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Paimon's glad to hear something sensible for once.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. About what we had discussed before... I did try, but I'm afraid I couldn't reach the old hag. I'll try again tonight, but I wouldn't get your hopes up...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Actually, someone already came over...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Mona about your mysterious guest...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Goodness gracious... Are you serious?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I believe she came to pass a message to us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She said that even the gods' gaze has blindspots — pretty bold if you ask Paimon. Most people would believe the gods to be all-knowing, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: The Hexenzirkel members are certainly anything but ordinary. As for the mage named N... The old hag has mentioned her a few times. She said that N's sense of direction is incredible, and that she loves guiding those who are lost.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: But I've never met her, and if she were still alive, she'd be... Well, suffice it to say that the hag's at least a few hundred now, and N's been around for longer than that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... The Hexenzirkel sounds like a scary group... But they must really stay in shape to live so long!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Their abilities alone are pretty terrifying. If she came to see you personally, then the problem you're facing must truly be of great importance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, it's not like Paimon could understand anything she said.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Yes, she was quite cryptic, but I suspect she means that there is still a way to turn things around. She didn't say when or what that would be, though, so...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Perhaps it is something that you cannot know right now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (True. Her words were meant as a helpful hint, but when will we realize their value and meaning...?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Was that the best answer that my question could have gotten?)

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, are you two alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we're fine, we're just a little down right now... It kinda feels like the end is coming, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I see. I feel that same sense of desperation, too.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I guess you could consider me someone who has often witnessed "fate." So far as I have seen, it cannot be swayed.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: But even so, I still hope for — and believe in — miracles. Astrology is eternal and rational, but fate may not be. It is cruel... but it can also be beautiful.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Perhaps that's what N was trying to tell you. Not to lose heart, and to believe that what you were seeing playing out before you is not yet set in stone.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I did originally think of steering clear of all this, but I couldn't. Even if this is all futile, I still wish to help everyone. If we don't struggle to the last, then how can we face the end when it comes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. You do have a point...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: *sigh* Haha, there I go talking about astrological principles again. Sorry about that, the moment I start talking about work-related stuff... Oh, I need to get going!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it, Mona — and thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: It was worth trying to comfort you, even if only a little. I believe that you'll help those who're struggling in the same way I did.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I suppose that might be why we always seem to meet by coincidence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon feels kinda moved by what Mona said... but also kinda sad, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}... Paimon suddenly feels like going outside for a walk. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Our names are written in this newspaper. Uh, what's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe we're famous?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "The underwater stronghold, the Fortress of Meropide, has continued in its noble autonomy, but that does not mean that others cannot interact with it."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "My recent attempts to enter the Fortress bore little fruit..." Huh? Guess Charlotte still hasn't given up on that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #"Thus did an outlander friend become the focus of this report — a {M#blond}{F#blonde} adventurer with their white fairy, legends trailing in their wake. It is said that this mysterious traveler once visited the underwater Fortress."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "So while the Fortress's interior remains a mystery behind closed doors, do not fear, for the tales of the Traveler contain surprises in spades!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Journalist Charlotte's biggest scoop yet — 'The Traveler's Trail: World-Walker.'"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Charlotte took so many awesome photos of us, and we never even noticed her!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She hasn't been able to get ahold of anything at the Fortress, so since we're easier to find, she's using us as the subject matter instead?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That sure seems to be the case...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, seriously... Well, fine. Those headlines and photos do look cool, so Paimon will forgive her this time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here! Phew, Paimon's hungry. Should we go in and get something to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, quick! Look... That's...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's the limited-edition, only 16-slices-a-day cake!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It hasn't already sold out for the day?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It was so delicious the last time we tried it, despite the tense situation we were in. Let's give it another go — Paimon's sure it'll be great!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can't let anyone get ahead of us!
One slice of cake, please.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Someone showed up after all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Wait, you're the one from the Palais Mermonia...

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: Oh, are you here to buy cake too? Haha, it seems Monsieur Neuvillette was right — you really can eat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, did he really say something like that?

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: That's right. Even he has his own preferences when it comes to food. As for me, I love the cake and coffee here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you come here often?

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: Mhm, usually every day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Every day...

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: It's part of my daily schedule apart from work — I shall have my cake and coffee.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then what if someone told you one day that this place would be closing soon, and you wouldn't get to eat cake here anymore? What would you think?

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: But why would it close?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon doesn't know either, but maybe... Maybe the waters will rise tomorrow... You know, like in the prophecy.

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: Oh, the prophecy... To be honest, I haven't paid much attention to that. No. Still, even if there'd be no more cake tomorrow, that wouldn't keep me from having some today.

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: No no. It's the same for eating in general. You might not be able to eat tomorrow, but if you can do so today, then you should carry on. That's what people call "living," you know?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh.

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: Don't be sad. Excuse me, could I have two more slices of cake to go?

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: These two slices are for you. Sigewinne said that this kind of expression you're making is what humans call "being sad."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you know Sigewinne?

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: I sure do. She was born before me, and she sometimes comes to the surface to teach us things about humans.

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: She said that humans are creatures that are saddened easily, yes, and you can only lift their spirits by feeding them delicious food — so, please try the cakes here.

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: I've got something else to do, so I'll be going now. You two try to stay in a good mood after eating, alright? Bye.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And there she goes...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's dig in. Paimon's sure this cake will be delicious.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You share a glance with Paimon and snarf down the cake.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's more delicious than last time — and the flavor gets even better with a sip of tea! It sure would be nice if we could come again tomorrow...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Sure would be nice if we could always eat delicious food here.
Ah, have you forgotten me already?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... You *are* familiar... You're the voice we heard from the sky in Sumeru!
"The voice from the sky," hmm? I fear that description is wrong — though not completely wrong.
You're feeling lost now, just as you were feeling previously. I sensed that confusion, and thus came to you. Guiding people is an irresistible hobby of mine, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you? And what do you want with us?
Consider me a passerby, just accepting a commission from my friend's disciple on a whim.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Friend's disciple... So, this is one of the friends of Mona's master? The enigmatic N of the Hexenzirkel?)

response.speaker: Mage "N"
response.text: The prophecy... Yes, what has been prophesized will be fulfilled. You may view such things as "the history of the future."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What... Th—Then, is there any way we can stop it?

response.speaker: Mage "N"
response.text: I believe you have witnessed a failed attempt with your own eyes. Can everything in Teyvat so easily be changed?

choices.text: Can there really be no exceptions?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: So she mentioned me? What did she say?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She said that you're a real "daredevil" of a journalist!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hahaha, nice — in which case, can this daredevil journalist dare to request an exclusive interview with the legendary Traveler and Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So your article in the paper today doesn't count?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Oh, of course it doesn't — that was more like live photography. What I'd like to do is dive deeper and ask you to talk about the things you've seen and experienced.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You seriously want to interview me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Are we even... qualified enough?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Why not? If I say you're worth an interview, then you're worth it! But not right now, of course. I'll need a few days to prepare.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, in that case, we'll just chat when you have time then?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: So that's a "yes"? Splendid! I'll tell the editor-in-chief immediately. I'll have to apply for lighting, a venue, some props, and...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Whew, so much to get done now. Talk to you later!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, Charlotte! Paimon's still got a question for you!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hmm? What's that...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If, just for example, Fontaine were to be flooded tomorrow, what would you do today?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Huh, that's the prophecy you're talking about, isn't it...? I mean, I do hear about it often, but I've never once thought that the day could be tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: If you're seriously asking, then I might try and think of a way to leave Fontaine. But I'm still a journalist first and foremost. That means I have a duty to be reporting from the scene. And secondly... I wouldn't forsake my homeland that easily.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: From what I've seen, most people don't know what they'd do should the worst come to pass. In truth, it might be better just to behave like normal rather than worry over such an end.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: So in all likelihood, I'd probably still be prepping at the office for that interview of ours. I know what you're thinking... that sounds a bit sad, but I've always believed that it's best to do what you enjoy.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Just think about it! If this nation really were to be suddenly destroyed tomorrow, but I still successfully finish an exclusive interview with a truly unique person, then the story I would wind up writing would truly be timeless.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: And then do you know what I'd do? Well, I'd write that story, send it for printing, and use messenger pigeons to get copies out to the various nations as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I'm not a dreamer, nor am I a workaholic, but I do love my job, and I'd be proud of leaving such an article behind. I guess you could say that I was born to be a journalist...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: But anyway, that's my answer — and on that note, I'll get back to my preparations!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's so nice. All of a sudden, Paimon actually kinda envies her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's go and take a look at the sea, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The sea breeze and scenery can be a pretty soothing combo, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's been thinking...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If it wasn't Fontaine, but all of Teyvat that would be destroyed tomorrow, where would we go, and what would we do?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, Paimon should ask, if you could choose, what would you like to do?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If I could choose, huh?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Hmm, it's just like Charlotte said... Suddenly trying to consider what to do is pointless.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've always been moving to the next destination, so we haven't spent much time thinking about these kinds of things. We didn't have to either, with us always being on the road and whatnot...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Until that moment comes, I think I'll keep journeying on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean still traveling?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. Wait, isn't that what we've always been doing?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The banter goes back and forth between the two of you as time slips by.\nAs night falls, you return to your accommodations and end this busy day.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The next few days are just as calm.\nCharlotte comes to find you and conducts the interview in the Spina di Rosula safehouse at the Fleuve Cendre.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Navia, having finished her business in Poisson, even drops by to take a photo with the two of you.\nAll goes well.

choices.text: That I have to look upon this world.

talks.objective: Go to the Spina di Rosula base

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn* Feels like you'll grow mold if you stay here long enough...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But it's still better than the Fortress of Meropide, that's for sure. It's not only damp there, but salty, too...

dialogues.speaker: Isadora
dialogues.text: Ah, so the two of you are still here. Wonderful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, you're from the Palais Mermonia, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Isadora
dialogues.text: Yes, I'm Isadora. Monsieur Neuvillette sent me to look for you two before... I heard that afterward, you went to the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Err... So are you under the impression that we might be wanted criminals?

dialogues.speaker: Isadora
dialogues.text: Haha, not at all. I'm well aware that you're friends of his. Actually, I'm here to pass along a message from him...

response.speaker: Isadora
response.text: Yes, inside the opera house. The Marechaussee Phantom has declared the incident a small-scale riot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A riot?

response.speaker: Isadora
response.text: Well, that said, I don't personally think it was that serious.

response.speaker: Isadora
response.text: Lady Furina was watching a performance at the opera house, and while she was resting during an intermission, some other audience members suddenly started harassing her...

response.speaker: Isadora
response.text: Loudly accusing her of doing nothing about the "prophecy crisis."

response.speaker: Isadora
response.text: And before she could respond, others started to join in.

response.speaker: Isadora
response.text: The crowd continued to grow and protests against the Hydro Archon started to break out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, people have started to put the blame on Furina... Guess they finally found an outlet for the pressure they've been under due to the prophecy.

response.speaker: Isadora
response.text: I agree. People will naturally rely on gods as is customary, but the moment people feel threatened, gods are also the first to be blamed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what happened after that? Is Furina okay?

response.speaker: Isadora
response.text: Seeing that the situation was spiraling out of control and that further argument was pointless, she claimed that she'd "gotten tired of this" and left in a hurry.

response.speaker: Isadora
response.text: The Marechaussee Phantom had their hands full maintaining order and did not catch where Lady Furina had gone. Only when things had stabilized did we realize that she had gone missing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, you mean she's still missing?

response.speaker: Isadora
response.text: That's right. The Marechaussee has dispatched many people to search for her, but we don't have any leads yet.

response.speaker: Isadora
response.text: That said, I don't think there's much to worry about. She is a god, after all. Even if she were to fall into the hands of rioters, what could ordinary people do to her?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I understand the situation.

response.speaker: Isadora
response.text: Good. Monsieur Neuvillette sent me to tell you about the situation, but he didn't say anything else...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, this is more than enough to go on. Thanks for keeping us informed!

response.speaker: Isadora
response.text: Ah, is that so? Well, alright then. In that case, you two take care. I'll be heading back to the Palais now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, sounds like we should hurry over to Poisson, then.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You sure caught on quickly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we know Furina, she won't try to fix things in this situation. Instead, she'll look for a place to wait out the heat.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And as we also know, she may be loud and dramatic, but she doesn't have a heart of stone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When Neuvillette was talking to her in the Palais Mermonia, and she heard about Poisson, she couldn't hide her sadness and remorse.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It would be hard for her to ignore being accused by the public today.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks Furina's probably taken the opportunity to slip away to Poisson and try to relieve the sense of guilt that she's feeling.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh... Well, whaddya think? Paimon knows the answer, of course, but Paimon can do the analysis to back it up too. Cool, huh?

choices.text: I see becoming a detective's done you some good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case, there's not a moment to lose. Poisson, here we come!

choices.text: Looks like those detective novels have had an effect on you.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Navia and Neuvillette both depart. You and Paimon head to the Spina di Rosula base at Fleuve Cendre...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, we're finally back!

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: Welcome back. We've got a special menu prepared for you two tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay, and there's good food, too! Navia — no, the Boss — is the best!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You did great as well, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, ooh, desserts! Nice! These are all Paimon's.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew! Paimon's already starting to forget what happened today...
Oh? That voice... Is that who I think it is?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: It's you two! What are you doing in Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mona!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did the stars not tell you that we might meet here?
Ah, have you forgotten me already?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, it's been a tough few days, hasn't it? So much has been happening!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Those meetings sure did make me hungry...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Paimon didn't think the meetings would go on for so long, but everyone seemed pretty fired up, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought they'd be at least a little frightened... Well, Freminet was, now that Paimon thinks about it. But everyone else just looked a little surprised.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you feel more confident after the meetings, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Well...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's hard to say — Paimon doesn't have any experience with this sort of thing. But with you around, Paimon's sure we'll do great!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After all, you're the most reliable person in the world, aren't you? Hehe... Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, did you just pour some tea? Paimon didn't notice you doing that at all!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, I didn't.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—Then what's that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Paimon's never seen that cup before!
Don't be frightened. I'm just joining you two for tea. I merely refrained from saying anything till now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Who's that voice!? But there's no one here!
What a strange conclusion, but also such an interesting one... You two make such a fascinating combo.
And yet, even you feel confused. As such, I couldn't resist but come by for some tea and a chat.

dialogues.text: Precisely. Call me N, a mage who wanders the world. At least, that's how my friends have suggested that I introduce myself.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The unexpected news leads to complicated feelings. You lie in bed for a long time before finally falling asleep.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: When you wake up, someone seems to be outside...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Paimon hears someone talking...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn*~ Alright, alright, coming...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're getting more diligent, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! It's you who's getting lazy, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Well, I see I've walked in on some lively banter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mona!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How've you been these past few days?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Fine, just fine. I went to take part in that Steambird panel. It turned out to be more interesting than I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Not all Fontainians are pessimistic about this. One journalist mentioned that sitting around and waiting for the end to come would be wrong, and that they should make their own rescue preparations. I agreed, so we had a brief chat with her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, did she have pink hair, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Why, yes — it was Charlotte! You remember her, right? That daredevil journalist?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I'm in full support of her view — prophecies are very important, but how can people allow their lives to be commandeered by just a few words?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Why, yes — it was Charlotte! I assume you've heard of her, no? That daredevil journalist?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I'm in full support of her view — prophecies are very important, but how can people allow their lives to be commandeered by just a few words?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: #Wow, if it isn't {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Have you seen the article I wrote about you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've got some nerve! You just used us to make some quick Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can we negotiate a profit split?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Oh, you needn't worry about that! I heard that you were in Poisson some time back, so I sent you a letter to discuss just that — it appears you didn't receive it, though.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: It's alright, though. I've set aside the amount intended for you. I've even set the table with some food!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Ooh, you're the best!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Heh, you're almost a little too easy to win over, Paimon. If I were a journalist with ulterior motives, you'd be in trouble now, you know!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon knows you're not like that!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Still, what brings you here all of a sudden? Were you looking for me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A friend of ours met you a while back, and when she mentioned it, we thought of coming to see you. Her name's Mona!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Ah, so you know Miss Mona as well? She's a guest columnist for our paper — a really good one, too! She's so young, and already such a brilliant astrologist!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When Mona mentioned you, we thought of coming to see you at work.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Haha, I see. It seems you've already bumped into Mona here in Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we're near the Steambird office. Let's go look for Charlotte and have a chat!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's take a walk around the city, shall we? There's a few spots we always like to walk by...
